summary.headline: Dharmaj Crop Guard cut FY27 growth guidance to single-digit from 18-20%, as Q2 revenue fell 4% to Rs 332.6 crore on a weak monsoon and technical slump.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 revenue held flat at Rs 716.7 crore and PAT rose 3% to Rs 51.3 crore, but Q2 revenue fell 4% YoY and EBITDA margin compressed to 7.3% from 9.2%. Management attributed the weakness to an 87% of LPA monsoon, a technical business down 27% in Q2 on West Asia-linked input cost and demand disruption, and higher raw material costs flowing through COGS. FY27 revenue guidance was reduced to single-digit growth from the earlier 18-20%. Management reiterated the Rs 2,000 crore revenue target for 2030 and said the herbicide facility remains on track.

segments.name: Institutional formulation
segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY in Q2 and 3% in H1; contributed 55% of H1 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Branded (blended) formulation
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY in Q2 and 2% in H1 as weak Kharif farmer consumption held back growth; contributed 19% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in Q2; H1 export grew 50% YoY to Rs 60 crore, now 8% of revenue vs 6% last year.

segments.name: Technical
segments.commentary: Revenue down 27% YoY in Q2 and 20% in H1 on West Asia-linked input pricing and demand disruption; 18% of H1 revenue vs 22% a year earlier. Production aligned to captive formulation needs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected to be single-digit, down from the earlier 18-20% guidance that assumed a normal monsoon.
Management expects to restore technical margins through cost pass-through to customers over Q3 FY27.
H2 focus: push higher exports, sustain domestic formulation, and restore technical margins.
Dharmaj 2030 target of Rs 2,000 crore revenue reconfirmed; management says it is on track, with about three years left.
Herbicide facility near Ahmedabad (Kerala GIDC) remains on track for commissioning, with production cycle ahead of next Kharif season.
capex_capacity: Capital work-in-progress Rs 11.7 crore at 30 Sep 2026 vs Rs 6.2 crore at March 2026, reflecting spend on the herbicide facility.
New herbicide facility to release capacity at the existing site; herbicide production cycle begins ahead of next Kharif.
Technical capacity aligned to captive formulation requirement to keep plant utilised; three new technical products added, with 2-3 products now backward-integrated.
demand_pricing: Monsoon rainfall at 87% of LPA per IMD, fourth lowest since 2001 and weakest since 2015; weakness concentrated in Western India.
Technical market hit by West Asia crisis affecting input prices and demand; merchant market realisation described as steady.
Raw material bought in March pre-Kharif protected Q1 margins; post-crisis purchases at higher prices flowed into Q2 COGS.
Operating expenses down 14% YoY to Rs 37.6 crore in Q2, partly offsetting gross margin compression.
Management says there is no sales return policy and no significant channel inventory issue.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for FY28 and how will formulation growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Agarwal said the weak season is rainfall-driven and the company remains on track for Rs 2,000 crore by 2030. Ramesh Talavia said the rainfall shortfall was mainly in Western India, with East and North not affected, and that the company will focus on recovering there.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be channel returns or inventory pressure given the sector downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said company policy is no sales returns and it controls this by working to need-based orders. He said there is no major inventory issue and that the company expects single-digit growth by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What technical molecules and geographies are targeted to support the Rs 2,000 crore vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said R&D and pilot work has added three new technical products, with 2-3 already backward-integrated. Priority is captive consumption for B2C and B2B formulations, with small technical sales. Export registrations have started coming in.

risks_watch: Single-digit FY27 growth implies a steep H2 ramp versus H1 flat revenue; monitor Q3 delivery.
Technical margin recovery depends on pricing pass-through, which management targets over Q3 FY27; watch gross margin trajectory from 18.6%.
Rabi season may be affected by weak monsoon and low reservoir levels, per management.
Herbicide facility commissioning timeline and its ramp-up before next Kharif.
Working capital: inventory fell to Rs 174 crore and receivables to Rs 409.9 crore; monitor for collection stress in a weak season.
Export momentum must be sustained to offset weak technical and branded volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term Rs 2,000 crore goal but clearly cautious on FY27, with guidance cut to single-digit growth. Management attributes the weakness to weather and the West Asia-driven technical slump, and pointed to cost pass-through and exports as H2 levers. Answers to the analyst's questions were somewhat generic and not supported by quantified plans.
key_quotes: Given this monsoon has turned out to be weakest in over a decade, Kharif demand has been subdued across the industry, and the technical market has not recovered in the way we had expected.
Our Dharmaj 2030 vision of Rs 2,000 crore top-line remains our central goal and we are on track to deliver it.
We are working to pass this higher cost on to end customers over Q3 and we accept technical margins to recover in coming quarters.
Our policy is that there is no sales return.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth cut to single-digit (from 18-20%) after Q2 revenue fell 4% on weak monsoon and a 27% technical slump; backing is a herbicide facility 'on track' with no specific capacity numbers, plus a Q3 cost pass-through in technical, with exports growing 50% in H1 but unquantified for the full year.
